The historical definition leaves the exact age-model formula, condition-column mapping and participant eligibility unbound; restore its named result without pretending those details are already qualified.
The paper reports 655 analyzed Salzburg recordings from 684 collected; the cohort is not age-diverse, with 423 participants younger than 30. Preserve its source population and interpretation.
Original numerical reference outputs, source-code/model parity and defensible reproduction acceptance criteria remain to be bound for the age analysis.
No authenticated ordered superiority criterion for the primary age-confound analysis is established. Larger coefficients, smaller p-values or better ECG decoding do not themselves demonstrate improvement.
Existing Figure 3 source components and reviewed scalar bookkeeping remain useful secondary evidence; their identity, native execution and verifier limitations remain.
No accepted explicit authority replacing the original primary was found in the inspected records. Current improvement rationale and REVIEW-rep014.json demonstrate a retargeting and internally reviewed TRF draft, not continuity with the retained original primary.
